ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.AnyEnemy)` (Hemokinesis.cs:20-23) == cost 1 / ATTACK / UNCOMMON / ANY_ENEMY.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new HpLossVar(2m)` + `new DamageVar(15m, ValueProp.Move)` (Hemokinesis.cs:14-18) == both numbers, both declared -- so `base_hp_loss` and `base_damage` both report correctly, unlike card/breakthrough's inlined HP loss.

OnPlay.rationale: Order matches: self-damage FIRST (`CreatureCmd.Damage(..., 2, Unblockable | Unpowered | Move, this)`, Hemokinesis.cs:28) == `DamageCmd.deal(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, self._hp_loss, card=self, props=DamageProps.CARD_HP_LOSS)`, then the attack (29-31). Crucially the self-damage goes through the full `DamageCmd.deal` pipeline here, so `on_damage_received` fires and RupturePower triggers -- exactly what card/breakthrough's hand-rolled HP loss fails to do. Presentation, folded in: WithHitFx.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Damage.UpgradeValueBy(5m)` (Hemokinesis.cs:36) == `self._damage += 5` (15 -> 20). The HP loss stays 2 when upgraded on both sides.

guards.what: the sim returns early on `if ctx.player.is_dead` between the HP loss and the attack (hemokinesis.py:38-39)
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-31 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 27.) The early return is DELETED. C# genuinely continues past the self-damage with no IsDead check (BloodWall.cs:36-40, Brand.cs:41-49, Hemokinesis.cs:28-31), and the sim now matches because every command the continued effect reaches ALREADY self-gates exactly as its C# counterpart does: BlockCmd.apply <-> CreatureCmd.GainBlock (CreatureCmd.cs:637-640, both IsOverOrEnding -> return 0); combat.select_cards <-> CardSelectCmd.FromHand (CardSelectCmd.cs:694-696, both -> []); PowerCmd.apply <-> PowerCmd.Apply<T> (PowerCmd.cs:69-72, both IsEnding -> null, already closed as power_cmd guard 1); DamageCmd.deal's dealer-dead bail <-> AttackCommand.Execute's IsOverOrEnding + Attacker.IsDead checks (AttackCommand.cs:520,528), both preceding Hook.BeforeAttack (:536). Death is synchronous on both sides -- C#'s Kill -> LoseCombat sets _pendingLoss before Damage() returns (CreatureCmd.cs:409,454; CombatManager.cs:945-950,180-220), which the sim's is_over_or_ending mirrors -- so the guard was provably redundant, not load-bearing. NOTE the recorded dependency was wrong: this did NOT need power/_death_prevention_branch (its remaining open sites are per-power revival paths; the generic _resolve_death arm no longer floors HP at 1). Pins: test/test_is_dead_early_returns.py (11).  The text it replaced read: Hemokinesis.cs has no such early return; C# would still run the attack command, which self-guards on `Attacker.IsDead` (AttackCommand.cs:528-531) and returns without hitting -- so the two actually agree on the attack itself. What C# still does and the sim skips is `Hook.BeforeAttack` / `AfterAttack` (AttackCommand.cs:536, 655), which fire around the no-op attack. DORMANT: the sim floors a death-prevented creature at 1 HP (cmds.py:106-112), so `is_dead` means the combat is already lost, and no ported before/after-attack listener acts after the player's death. Same family as card/blood_wall's and card/bloodletting's guards (rule 3).
